correctness.rationale: The source full text was checked for all nonstandard inputs: Theorem 1 gives arbitrarily long steady words over four letters, Theorem 3 states that every steady word over a fixed alphabet of at least three letters is bifurcate, and Conjecture 2 asks for an infinite quaternary bifurcate chain under single-letter extension. The new lemma is exact: if U is a factor of steady W, then every one-letter deletion of U is a factor of the corresponding deletion of W, hence is square-free. Thus steady words are prefix-closed. Their fixed-alphabet prefix tree is finitely branching and has unbounded depth, so König's infinity lemma gives an infinite ray. Every factor of the ray lies in a steady prefix and is therefore steady, and Theorem 3 makes every such factor bifurcate.

value.rationale: The claim settles an explicit published conjecture at the sharp alphabet size four. It also gives a stronger coherent object: one infinite quaternary word every finite factor of which is steady, hence bifurcate. The proof identifies a structural property—factor heredity of steadiness—that turns the paper's unbounded finite existence theorem into an infinite nested object by compactness. This is a genuine conceptual closure of a stated research gap rather than a routine finite increment.
